props.name: methanol formed came from actual synthesis (blank)
props.statement: With no catalyst in the reactor no condensate was obtained, showing that the small amounts of methanol formed were due to actual synthesis.

props.name: none of the catalysts was specific for methanol synthesis
props.statement: None of the catalysts used was specific for the reaction CO + 2H2 = CH3OH.

props.name: condensates essentially methanol and water
props.statement: Fractionation of the combined water layers of all condensates gave 1.6 cc. of methanol (b.p. 64°) with no appreciable n-propanol, so the condensates were essentially methanol and water; the oil layer (initial b.p. 102°) contained no methanol.

props.name: the earlier paper's equations give only order-of-magnitude Kp
props.note: concerns the authors' own earlier paper (This Journal, 55, 4747 (1933))
props.statement: Because the thermal data for formaldehyde are so doubtful, the equations of the authors' earlier paper give only order-of-magnitude values, and Kp for methanol synthesis derived from them would be far less accurate than direct measurement.

props.name: equation D best represents the measured points
props.statement: The averages measured in this work agree excellently with equation D, and since D fits the other investigators' values as well as any of the equations, it appears to be the best representation of the points.

props.name: equation D is largely empirical
props.statement: Equation D must be regarded largely as an empirical equation which best represents the experimental points.

props.name: the fit of D is no proof of its thermal data
props.statement: That equation D fits the experimental points better than the other equations is no proof of the greater accuracy of its thermal data; e.g. D uses Thomsen's heat of combustion of CO, whereas Rossini's value is believed more accurate.

props.name: catalyst temperature uniform and steady within 0.1°
props.statement: The temperature throughout the catalyst bed did not vary more than 0.1° from the Table II figure, nor with time more than 0.1°.

props.name: an alternative methanol heat capacity changes the curves only slightly
props.statement: The molal heat capacity of methanol vapour is somewhat in doubt, but using Francis's equation changes the location and slope of the curves only very slightly.

props.name: colorimetric and titration methods agree
props.statement: The excellent checks between the colorimetric and titration methods for methanol further indicate the absence of compounds other than methanol and water.

props.name: closer agreement requires a much more specific catalyst
props.statement: Closer agreement among measured values of the methanol equilibrium constant appears impossible until a much more specific catalyst is found.

props.name: methyl formate absent from the condensates
props.note: how it was shown is not described in this paper
props.statement: Methyl formate was shown to be absent from the condensates.

props.name: the 3 atm pressure correction (1.5% at 250°) is negligible
props.statement: The deviation of the equilibrium constant at three atmospheres from Kp0 is 1.5% at 250°, negligible compared with experimental errors, so no pressure correction was applied.

props.name: measured values at 225-275° and 3 atm agree with equation D

props.statement: The four equations show how much spread is produced merely by different choices of thermal data; even extremely accurate equilibrium data would not single out any particular datum, because each equation combines several data.
